ov: Land-living turtles with domed shells and column-like, elephant-like legs. They are slow, placid plant-eaters, and most species can live 80–150 years.
len: Up to more than 1.2 m (Galápagos giant tortoise)
wt: Over 100 kg (Galápagos and Aldabra giant tortoises)
df: Mostly plants. Young tortoises of herbivorous species also eat worms and insect larvae for protein.

cf.tip: All tortoises are turtles, but tortoises are the land specialists, with column-like legs and elephant-like feet instead of flippers.

fx: An Aldabra giant tortoise named Adwaita may have lived an estimated 255 years.
